newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares weaker, focus on Lisnave.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares weaker, focus on Lisnave.

text.p: Portuguese shares ended weaker with activity focused on ship repairer Lisnave which tumbled after it announced its restructuring plans. The fall in foreign markets weakened Portugal Telecom and Sonae Investimentos, dealers said. Other active stocks included Banco Portugues de Investimento and Banco Comercial Portugues.
Dealers said they expected a quiet session tomorrow amid selective trade.
Loss-making ship repairer Lisnave said it would be split into two companies under a restructuring that will involve a drastic reduction in its capital.
Shares of Lisnave tumbled 43 percent in morning trade following the statement by the company in the local press.
Lisnave said it would be split into one company that will carry on ship repairing activities and another that will try to find jobs for the excess labour of the group.
The two new companies will each have a capital of 3.6 billion escudos. Lisnave presently has a capital of 35.6 billion.

Pulp group Portucel Industrial (PI) is expected to post a loss of between 1.4 and 1.8 billion escudos in 1996 because of drops in pulp prices, but should recover to make a profit in 1997, analysts said.
PI is expected to distribute a dividend of between eight and 20 escudos per share for 1996 when it announces its results on February 25, they said.
